nodes.title: Length
widgets_values:
### Length

Read from the clay video, rounded **down** to H3's grid:

90 · 107 · 124 · 141 · 158 · 175 · 192 · 209 · 226 · 243 ... 362

Down, so the reference covers the whole clip. The rest is dropped. Trim the
pass to a grid value if you need all of it.

**Clay pass must be 24 fps.** Anything else gets squeezed in time and the
motion drifts off your original.

**Look plate is a still**, not a frame from the clay video. It sets material
and colour, not layout.

nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
# AI RENDERER
## MiniMax H3

Clay render in, finished shot out. The video gives the motion, the reference
image gives the look.

1. Load the models (group 1)
2. Load your clay video and look plate (group 4)
3. Edit the prompt (group 5), keep the `<Video 1>` and `<Picture 1>` tags
4. Run

**Custom nodes**

* [KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes) - Set/Get
* [VideoHelperSuite](https://github.com/Kosinkadink/ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite) - Load Video
* [Mickmumpitz Nodes](https://github.com/mickmumpitz/ComfyUI-Mickmumpitz-Nodes) - labels, resolution

Needs ComfyUI 0.30.1 or newer.

nodes.title: Prompt
widgets_values:
### Prompt

`<Picture 1>` is the look plate, `<Video 1>` is the clay pass. Numbers count
per type, in input order: images first, then videos. Keep both tags.

* **Instructions work, bans do not.** "no camera move" does nothing. Write
  "one continuous take" instead. A written `CUT` marker does work.
* **`Timeline:` must reach the end of the clip.** If it stops early, picture
  and sound trail off.

### Example

nodes.title: Steps
widgets_values:
### Steps

**4** with the LoRA. 6 costs 44 % more time and looks the same.

**20** without it, sampler `res_multistep`. Slower, more faithful, softer.
The turbo LoRA oversharpens.

To switch: Ctrl+B the LoRA in group 2, steps to 20, sampler to
`res_multistep`.

nodes.title: Audio
widgets_values:
### Audio

Off by default. Switched on it feeds `ref_video_audio_0`, so it hangs off the
first reference video.

* **Voice only carries over that way.** Standalone `ref_audio` does nothing
  for speech.
* **Pad the recording with silence to the exact clip length.** A clip longer
  than the audio gets filled, usually by repeating your line.
* Pick the grid length just above your recording and pad up to it.
* **Put the spoken line in the prompt too**, in quotes, plus "once and only
  once".
* **Speech start moves with the seed.** Render dialogue twice and pick.

Or skip this node and use the clay video's own sound: `audio` output on the
left.

### SeedVR2 upscale

Pulls the render up to 2K and invents detail that was not there: spray becomes
single droplets, foam becomes structure.

**`resolution` is the short edge**, not the long one. Aspect ratio is kept.
From a 1344x768 render:

| short edge | gives |
|---|---|
| 768 | 1344 x 768 (unchanged) |
| **1170** | **2046 x 1170** (preset, 2K) |
| 1440 | 2520 x 1440 |
| 2048 | 3584 x 2048 (4K) |

**`batch_size` must be 4n+1**: 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 33. Bigger buys temporal
consistency and costs VRAM. Preset is **9**. Drop to 5 or 1 on a smaller card.

**4K is three times the pixels of 2K** and does not fit on most cards. Try it
only with a lot of headroom, and expect a long wait before it fails.

**Check the short edge against your render.** At scale 1.5x the render is
already 1152 tall, so 1170 does almost nothing. Raise it or skip the group.

Bypass this group if you only want the look. Group 6 saves the plain render
either way.

**H3 works in 1.75, not 16:9.** That is why 1170 gives 2046 and not 2080.
